title: Compass — Agentic Task & Work Management
summary: Compass is David Holt's task and work-management system, built to be operated by an agent as much as by a human. It isn't a UI you'd describe to someone — it's an MCP tool surface. Once an agent is connected (see 'connect'), it can read and write a user's real Compass account directly: create tasks, log CRM activity, move content through a pipeline, plan weeks, score priorities, all as tool calls, no page-clicking involved.

what_a_connected_agent_can_do.tasks: Create, list, update, and delete tasks and subtasks. Score a task's priority. Set its status (see 'status_values' — this is the one piece of Compass's data model an agent needs to know to use the tools correctly).
what_a_connected_agent_can_do.crm: Track people and contacts, log completed activities, create follow-ups, and pull activity reports.
what_a_connected_agent_can_do.content_pipeline: Move a piece of content through topic -> framework -> draft -> final draft -> post, creating and updating each stage.
what_a_connected_agent_can_do.frameworks: Create and manage reusable frameworks/templates for recurring work.
what_a_connected_agent_can_do.use_cases: Track use-case patterns and their instances.
what_a_connected_agent_can_do.week_planning: Define week templates and week block types, and create scheduled blocks of time.
what_a_connected_agent_can_do.priority_matrix: Score competing tasks against personal or business trade-off models.
what_a_connected_agent_can_do.onboarding: Fetch live onboarding guidance immediately after connecting — tells the agent whether this looks like a fresh account worth offering to import tasks into, and how to map them in.
what_a_connected_agent_can_do.account: Check who the connection is authenticated as, review AI activity/settings, and sign out (revokes the token) if the user asks to disconnect.

status_values.WAITING: Hidden from working views until its follow-up date arrives.

if_not_connected_yet: Most of the above requires an authenticated MCP connection to this user's account. If you don't have one, the simple route is adding Compass as a connector directly in your client's own settings, pointed at mcp_endpoint — the client handles sign-in itself. See agents/compass-signin.json for that walkthrough, plus an alternative agentic pairing option for chat surfaces without connector settings of their own.
author: David Holt
